name: Rietz
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village in the Oberinntal with a beautiful parish church and the perfect starting point for hikes into the surrounding forests.
text:
Überblick

Rietz is situated in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley within the Imst district at an altitude of 677 metres on a sunny terrace on the northern banks of the Inn River, home to around 2,520 residents. The municipality nestles beneath the commanding Rietzer Grießkogel peak, which towers to 2,884 metres within the northern Stubai Alps. Rietz forms a geographic gateway between greater Innsbruck and the Tyrolean Oberland, located between the market town of Telfs to the east and Stams to the west. Benefiting from a mild valley floor climate, Rietz features productive fruit orchards and agriculture. Known as Tyrol's Village of Churches, it charms visitors with sacred treasures, carnival traditions, and alpine hiking.

Geschichte

Rietz was first recorded in official documents in 1264. The municipal coat of arms displays three white churches on a green three-peaked hill, symbolizing the community's extraordinary wealth of religious architecture. Alongside farming, bobbin lace-making and rosary-chain linking were vital cottage industries for generations. The town's prominent landmark is the pilgrimage church of St. Anthony of Padua, perched high on the Scheibenbichl hill. Founded in 1676 following a vow by court messenger Peter Grasmayr, it was rebuilt between 1743 and 1757 by Johann Michael Umhauser as an ornate rococo sanctuary with a calvary path. The oldest sanctuary is the parish church of St. Valentine with Gothic choirs, while the Kreuzkirche church in the lower village commemorates a 1622 plague deliverance vow.

Anreise

Rietz is ideally linked to transportation corridors. By car, drivers leave the Inntalautobahn A12 at exit Telfs-West or Mötz/Stams and follow the B171 Tiroler Straße for a few minutes directly into the village centre. Rail travellers take the S-Bahn Tirol (lines S4 and S5) along the Arlberg railway to the Rietz in Tirol railway station, served every thirty minutes. Furthermore, frequent VVT regional buses connect Rietz with Telfs, Stams, and Imst.

Tipps

A walk to the pilgrimage church of St. Anthony on the Rietzer Berg hill rewards guests with a sweeping 360-degree panoramic view across the Inn Valley and the Mieming Range. Experienced mountaineers can embark on the challenging alpine trek up the 2,884-metre Rietzer Grießkogel via the Peter-Anich-Hütte refuge and the pristine Angersee lake. Along the river banks runs the flat Inn-Radweg cycle trail, perfect for relaxed cycling. Climbers find compact limestone crags nearby at the Klettergarten Stams climbing area. Just five kilometres west, the historic Cistercian Stift Stams abbey showcases baroque basilicas and museum collections. In the village, the local heritage museum illustrates centuries of craft work and carnival customs.
